Historical Shawnee village

Peckuwe

Peckuwe was a Shawnee village in the Mad River valley near present-day Springfield, Ohio. George Rogers Clark Park preserves part of its setting.

Selected reading

01

The Mad River village

The park district identifies Peckuwe with the site of today’s George Rogers Clark Park. Wright State University’s field-school report places the village near the Mad River and records the spellings Piqua and Picawey for the same village in this account.

Read the sources [1] National Trail Parks & Recreation District [2] Wright State University

02

The 1780 attack

The park district describes a 1780 attack by troops led by George Rogers Clark that drove Shawnee people from the village.

Read the sources [1] National Trail Parks & Recreation District

Foundation find ↗

Wright State’s account of its archaeology field school places the village near the Mad River and records the forms Peckuwe, Piqua, and Picawey in this setting.

Inspection: Supporting or limited review; see scope

Scope: The field-school report’s George Rogers Clark Park and Mad River references and its identification of the 1780 Shawnee village.

Review recorded: November 20, 2026
